messages:
Alex: Heads-up — I've been digging into the slot fragmentation on hetero nodes (A100/RTX mix) in eu-west1. Latency SLOs for latency-sensitive tenants keep getting bumped when we pack them on RTXs that also serve batch jobs.
Priya: Ugh. Seen similar in eu-central last week. Is this the same noisy-neighbor pattern or more of a placement + hetero-capacity mismatch?
Alex: Leaning toward placement mismatch + scheduler blind to GPU-class affinity. Noisy neighbor is part of it — batch tails stalling PCIe and hogging NVLink, but primarily the scheduler is putting low-prio batch on the same physical MIGs as p99-sensitive jobs.
Mateo: Can we flag tenants by "latency_profile" and have a soft-silo for latency-sensitive ones (dedicated slices of A100) vs best-effort RTX pool? Means adding a routing tag + fallback logic.
Hana: That would help, but cost hit will be visible. Many tenants currently on shared capacity would need reserved slices. How bad is the utilization delta?
Alex: Quick sim: if we carve 20% of A100 capacity into low-concurrency latency silos, utilization drops ~12% but p99 improves 40-60ms across affected tenants. Worth for enterprise SLAs.
Priya: Sounds reasonable for premium tiers. We should avoid rigid static partitioning — prefer dynamic soft-silos where autoscaler can reassign whole nodes between pools during nights.
Jess: Agree. Also propose a routing policy: prefer node with matching GPU_class tag, else prefer same-customer isolation if tenant marked "sensitive=true". Implement as 3-step: exact-tag -> isolated-node -> shared-fallback.
Mateo: Implementation notes: need scheduler changes + admission check to refuse placement if fallback would violate p99 budget. Also need to expose a new pool type in console and billing impact in cost breakdown.
Alex: infra-bot: create ticket for 'hetero-siloing routing policy' and attach sim graphs
infra-bot: Ticket #INF-4721 created: hetero-siloing routing policy — link: https://go/infra/INF-4721
Priya: We should prototype with a canary: pick 5 enterprise tenants, mark them sensitive, and route to soft-silos in us-west2 only. Watch egress, p99, and token cost. Can we do a controlled rollback?
Jess: Yes — rollout plan in the ticket: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> global. Each step has automated rollback if p99 regresses >10% or cost per token increases >15%.
Mateo: For the scheduler change, here's a minimal config snippet we can use in the canary:```yaml
placement_policy:
  - prefer: gpu_class
  - require: tenant_isolation:false
  - fallback: shared_pool
  - max_retries: 2
```
Hana: Watch AZ-spread implications. If we silo too strictly by gpu_class we risk AZ fragmentation and cross-AZ egress. Add an AZ-balancing constraint in the policy.
Alex: Good call. Add a constraint: "prefer_same_az: true" with a lower weight than gpu_class so we don't break the affinity chain.
Priya: Who wants action items? I can own canary orchestration + dashboards. Alex can do the scheduler patch. Mateo, can you run the sim for utilization vs cost? Jess add rollout docs + billing changes. Hana will monitor AZ/egress impact.
Alex: Works for me. Starting PR draft now.
Mateo: I'll push sim results by EOD tomorrow.
Jess: I'll update the console mockups and billing impact table.
Hana: I'll wire up alerting for cross-AZ egress anomalies.
Priya: Thanks all. Quick note: keep the fallback path because some tenants must never be siloed (cost-sensitive dev orgs). We'll keep a tenant tag to opt-out.
Alex: Yup — opt-out tag added to the proposal.
Jess: :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Deploy job queued for INF-4721 canary sandbox.
Alex: Thread wrap — we'll meet tomorrow 10:30 to review sim + canary plan.
